setting: A student reserves a group study room and learns the rules about no-shows and equipment.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a library staff member.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi. I need a group study room for four people tomorrow evening. We're preparing a presentation.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Rooms book in two-hour blocks. I have 6 to 8 p.m. in room 214, or 7 to 9 in room 301—301 has a large display screen.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: 301, please. Do we need to bring our own HDMI cable?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: There's a cable in the drawer, but check it when you arrive. If it's missing, borrow one at the desk with your ID.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: What if one person is late? Last time we lost a room for a no-show.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Someone from your group must check in at the desk within ten minutes of the start time, or the reservation is released.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Covered drinks are fine. No messy food—crumbs attract pests and you'll lose booking privileges for two weeks.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Understood. Can I extend the booking if another group doesn't show?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Only at the desk after your first hour, and only if the next slot is free. I can't promise it in advance.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Okay. Please put it under Maya Chen, ID ending in 4421.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.A: Paying an overdue fine for a laptop
options.B: Booking a group study room and following its rules
options.C: Moving books to the quiet floor
options.D: Applying for a library student job

questions.explanation: She reserves room 301 and learns check-in, food, cable, and extension rules.

questions.narrator_text: Which room does she choose and why is it useful?

options.A: 214, because it is closer to the entrance
options.B: 301, because it has a large display screen
options.C: The cafe area, because food is allowed

questions.explanation: She picks 301 for the large display screen (7–9 p.m.).
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—214 was offered but she selects 301.

questions.narrator_text: What must the group do to keep the reservation?

options.A: Email the librarian the night before
options.B: Check in at the desk within ten minutes of the start time
options.C: Leave a cash deposit at room 214
options.D: Arrive with all four members at once

questions.explanation: Someone must check in within ten minutes or the room is released.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing D—only someone from the group must check in, not necessarily all four at once.

questions.narrator_text: What is the policy on food?

options.B: Covered drinks are fine, but messy food can cost booking privileges for two weeks
options.C: Only food from the library cafe is allowed inside rooms

questions.explanation: Covered drinks OK; messy food risks losing booking privileges for two weeks.
